bib.title: Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing? Catastrophic Remembering in Agentic Coding

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing? Catastrophic Remembering in Agentic Coding", Kushal Chakrabarti (South Park Commons, sole author), arXiv:2608.11095v1 [cs.AI], 11 Aug 2026. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

COVERAGE: All 24 pages read (98,842 chars): body, limitations, ethics, appendices A-E (skimmed the reference list and some appendix tables). Extraction clean. No embedded instructions.

CORE CLAIM: Agent context files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md) grow without bound because the reason behind each instruction is never written down and is forgotten. Deleting an instruction without a regression then needs an infeasible number of counterfactual probes, so people only add. The author calls this "catastrophic remembering". The fix he tests is a "prompt comment": a note to the next maintainer, stripped before the executor sees it, recording why the instruction exists, what failed and what happened.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
- Observational (Sec 3): 1,867 public GitHub repos, 247,694 instruction lifetimes. Instruction count grows +226% over a file's lifetime. The median file holds 39 instructions at its last version (p90 131). Net +4.9 instructions per commit across 19,267 commits.
- Of the repos with several versions, 64.3% grew and 26.6% shrank (n=1,576).
- Deletion hazard falls with age: log-hazard slope -0.032/commit, 95% CI [-0.047,-0.019] (28,426 deletions). That falsifies the "instructions go stale" explanation. A gamma-frailty refit leaves the slope at -0.0355.
- 77.3% of instruction deaths happen in a wholesale rewrite or file migration. A rewrite cuts the file to 59.5%, it regrows to 91.5% within 10 commits, and regrowth is faster afterwards (4.9% vs 4.1% per commit; 52 files).
- Controlled (Sec 4.2, Table 2): IFEval inverted so the optimal prompt is known. Maintainer and executor are both claude-haiku-4-5, with the maintainer's task stated only as a brief objective (the benchmark's own instructions hidden). At T=15, 552 histories, 3 seeds: excess size +60.4% without comments, -5.8% with informative comments, +53.2% with comment-shaped noise. Constraint satisfaction is at parity (39.0 vs 38.2%). At T=51, 184 worlds, 1 seed: +211.3% falls to +1.4%, which is the "99.3% of excess removed" figure.
- Capability (Table 9, Haiku 4.5 executor, 64 worlds, 1 seed): the uncommented arm's excess grows with a stronger maintainer (+67.7% to +571.9%), and comments help more.
- Ablation (Table 10, 64 worlds, 1 seed): comments must carry outcomes. A narrative of attempts without outcomes is the worst arm (+70.0%).
- WildIFEval (Sec 4.3): 64 worlds, 16 noisy distractor instructions seeded in, claude-haiku-4-5 judge. The noise cost 24.1pp of correctness (65.6% to 41.5%). Comments lifted satisfaction from 50.4% to 62.0% (+11.6pp, 95% CI [5.1,18.3]), a 23.1% relative gain.

QUOTES
- p1: "agentic prompts grow without bound, more than tripling over their lifetime (+226%), gaining +4.9 net instructions every commit"
- p2: "An instruction tells the executor what to do; a comment tells the next maintainer why." (Sec 4.1, p6)
- p2: "76.8% of instruction deaths arrive in one commit that bulldozes the file, after which growth resumes at its prior rate" (Section 3.2 on p5 gives 77.3% for rewrite plus migration)
- p9, Limitations: "covers of two or three instructions against a median file's 39, a 15-step horizon, one model as both maintainer and executor, mechanically verifiable English constraints"

LIMITS (conceded or visible)
- The controlled experiment is a synthetic maintainer loop on IFEval-style constraints. Covers are 2-3 instructions against a real median of 39. It is not real repositories, real coding tasks or human maintainers. It uses one small model (Haiku 4.5).
- Only T=15 has 3 seeds. The T=51 headline (99.3%) is a single seed with a wide CI (+1.4±22.1). Tables 9 and 10 are single-seed with n=64.
- The arms separate only under a tuned regime of five conditions (vague verdicts, censored passes, hidden constraint ids, no brevity objective, at least 10 steps). The author "found this regime by search". If the verifier spec is disclosed, the effect vanishes (+3.0% excess, no effect).
- The protocol empties about 1 prompt in 8, and satisfaction parity fails on those worlds. The author warns to keep a person in the deletion path and hold safety-relevant instructions out of scope.
- WildIFEval is scored by an LLM judge. A second judge gives +7.8pp, whose difference from 11.6pp does not exclude zero. Neither judge is ground truth.
- The repo analysis is observational: no causal test on real files, a matcher validated on only 50 hand-annotated transitions (author-annotated), and English only. Whether it applies to system prompts or skill files is open. The "imperfect recall" mechanism is inferred from the hazard slope and author count. Nobody tested it by intervention in real repos.
- The paper never tests comments in a real CLAUDE.md. The prototype is "just a prototype". No test shows whether real agents handle deletion or comments well.
- The author used LLMs heavily for writing, code and appendix text.

BUILDS ON
- Chatlatanagulchai et al. 2025 (arXiv:2511.12884, Agent READMEs), Tafreshipour et al. 2025 and Lulla et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.20404): AGENTS.md files help and only grow.
- FollowBench (Jiang et al., ACL 2024), WildIFEval (Lior et al. 2025) and IFEval (Zhou et al. 2023): instruction-following degrades as constraints accumulate.
- Organizational rule-change theory (March, Schulz and Zhou 2000; Zhou 1993; Schulz 1998).
- Comment-the-why practice (Knuth 1984; McConnell 2004; LaToza et al., ICSE 2006) and architecture decision records (Nygard 2011).
- Catastrophic forgetting (McCloskey and Cohen 1989; Kirkpatrick et al., PNAS 2017).
- Memory systems (MemGPT, Mem0, Zep), which evict on staleness proxies.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: p1, Figure 1 "(a) Causal: Prompts without comments (or with comment-shaped noise) grow without bound; with informative comments, they settle near the optimal size... (b) Observational: ... number of prompt instructions in an agentic README more than triples (+226%)". Alternative: p4 Figure 4, the rewrite ratchet.

ASSESSMENT: The observational half (growth, rewrites, falling hazard) is reasonably strong evidence that entry files accumulate and are rarely pruned. It is relevant to note 09 for the "entry file bloat" and "record the why" points. The remedy evidence is weak and indirect: synthetic, single small model, partly single-seed, and it measures instruction-following, not task success. Cite the growth finding with its setup. Cite the comment benefit only as a simulated result, and do not present it as validated advice for real CLAUDE.md files.
